results.title: Mixed Research Method Design - an overview
results.content: For example, a mixed methods research approach could utilize qualitative methods (e.g., case studies, ethnographies) to collect information about community members’ views throughout the research process and quantitative methods (e.g., surveys of larger samples of community members, constituents, or program advisors; random assignment experimental designs) to speak to the robustness of study findings (Mertens, 2007). Mixed methods researchers also must make decisions about the pacing and implementation of the quantitative and qualitative portions of the study, including the timing of data collection, analysis, and use of results (Creswell & Plano Clark, 2011). In some situations, the researcher may implement a study with multiple phases that include both concurrent and sequential timing of the qualitative and quantitative portions (see Creswell & Plano Clark, 2011 for a detailed discussion of the relative merits and challenges with various mixed methods research designs). Mixed methods researchers systematically collect quantitative and qualitative data and analyze them in an integrative manner in a single study (Tashakkori et al., 2021).
